subject: Cutover acceptance + contingency scenarios for offline build rollouts
messages:

Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com

Subject: Initial acceptance window and contingency plan for Sept islanded rollout

Hi Sergio / Kimberly,

Thanks again for walking through the packaging options last week. We’ve finalized the offline artifact bundle for the EdgeOps islanded DC (bundle v2026-09-14). Attached is the release-manifest and the SHA manifest that our courier will carry. Two quick asks before we kick off acceptance:

- Can Redwood confirm the expected operator key rotation step IDs so we can mirror them on our side?
- We want a short contingency runbook for the event the signed bundle fails verification onsite (network still isolated). Can you sketch the minimum manual validation + rollback sequence you expect operators to perform?

We propose an acceptance window on Sep 22 UTC (08:00–12:00 local) with a 2-hour dry-run the prior day. If that works I’ll route the courier and upload the signed media manifest to your DocuSign envelope.

Attachments: release-manifest-2026-09-15.json, signed-bundle-20260914.sha256

Thanks,
Matt Collins
Head of Field Ops — EdgeOps Systems
matt.collins@edge-ops.io
+1 (415) 555-0108
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Matt Collins <matt.collins@edge-ops.io>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-15T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial acceptance window and contingency plan for Sept islanded rollout

Matt — thanks for the artifacts and heads-up. Good data to start with. High-level answers below; I’ll follow up with a brief checklist we expect operators to have.

- Operator key rotation: we use a two-step activation. Step A (pre-validate) verifies bundle signature against the central signing key thumbprint. Step B (activation) rotates the operator signing key after acceptance and records an activation checkpoint in the local audit log. We’ll send you the step IDs and the expected HSM nonce exchange snippet.

- Offline verification failure (contingency): we prefer a deterministic rollback to the prior signed bundle. Sequence: 1) run offline-verify.sh (hash check + signature verify); 2) if verify fails, run inspect-manifest to get failed file list; 3) attempt on-site local signature re-check using cached root certificate (we will ship root cert with the media); 4) if still failing, run bundle-rollback --target <previous-build> and open an incident to Redwood infra so we can fetch a replacement signed bundle via a courier.

The Sep 22 window is acceptable. Dry-run on Sep 21 at 10:00 PT looks good for our on-call team.

I’ll attach the operator checklist and the minimal command snippets in a follow-on.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, Matt Collins <matt.collins@edge-ops.io>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-15T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial acceptance window and contingency plan for Sept islanded rollout

Adding a few operational constraints that matter for the dry-run and the contingency steps:

- On the dry-run we will not perform key rotation (no activation). Dry-run validates signature, file integrity, and preflight checks only.
- The onsite operator will need a USB with the root cert plus a portable verification VM image (we will provide).
- If a rollback is needed and the courier is already en route, please ensure the courier manifest includes a clear previous-build label and an explicit chain-of-custody handoff location (we’ve had confusion in the past when manifests used build tags only).

I’ve attached version 2 of our acceptance checklist (acceptance-checklist-v2.xlsx) that includes the verbatim commands for the operator VM and the minimum telemetry we expect to be pushed to Redwood once the site is reconnected.

- Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: Matt Collins <matt.collins@edge-ops.io>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com

Thanks Kim — that checklist looks comprehensive. A couple clarifying points from Ops:

1) Courier manifest: we can include both the build tag and the prior-build tag on the physical manifest placard; good call to have both.
2) Verification VM: can you confirm the VM image hash so our provisioning team can burn it to the USB?

We’ll proceed with the dry-run on Sep 21 10:00 PT and keep the carrier on standby for Sep 22 acceptance. I’ll upload the DocuSign envelope once we agree on the exact signature thumbprint and the HSM nonce exchange string.

Matt

Subject: Re: Initial acceptance window and contingency plan for Sept islanded rollout — final confirmations

Quick final notes before the dry-run:

- Vanessa will run the verification test with Matt’s provisioning team tomorrow Sep 20 at 09:30 PT to confirm the USB image hash and VM boot behavior.
- SOP for failed verification (compressed checklist):
  1) Confirm hash mismatch with offline-verify.sh and log output.
  2) Attempt re-verify with cached root cert (root_cert.pem) included in the media.
  3) If still failing, run bundle-rollback --target v2026-08-30 and set operator flag --require-signer-recheck to force audit mode.
  4) Notify Redwood infra pager and mark the site as "restricted" until replacement media arrives.

- Evidence for compliance: we will ask the onsite operator to capture the verification output, a photo of the courier seal, and the manifest placard. These artifacts can be uploaded to the DocuSign envelope or the Confluence page after the site re-connects.

I’ve added OpsSite Security on cc so they can review the contingency steps related to chain-of-custody handling. If there are no objections, I’ll lock the acceptance window and send calendar invites for the dry-run and the acceptance window.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Program Manager, Field Deployments — Redwood Inference
